note: Unselected T2D; none of the seven members (teneligliptin, omarigliptin, prusogliptin, cofrogliptin, retagliptin, besigliptin, melogliptin) holds a US NDA, so there is no FDA review package and the model side rests on the sponsors' pharmacology papers; sitagliptin and the other first-wave gliptins are siblings, not members, and do not score.
label: Type 2 diabetes (DPP-4)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; Mitsubishi Tanabe authors. The Zucker fatty rat work predates the 2012 Japanese approval but was published after it; model_filed is null because the PMDA review is not in the bundle.
engagement.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
engagement.note: Teneligliptin inhibited rat plasma DPP-4 (ED50 0.41 mg/kg) and raised active GLP-1 and insulin after a carbohydrate load in Zucker fatty rats; nothing compared yet.
engagement.quote: Oral administration of teneligliptin in Wistar rats resulted in the inhibition of plasma DPP-4 with an ED(50) of 0.41 mg/kg.
engagement.judgement: Pooled as one track: every member's pharmacology paper uses the same assay (ex-vivo plasma DPP-4 activity plus an oral glucose or carbohydrate load) in a rodent, the strain varying; the earliest member publication (teneligliptin, 2012) opens the strip.

engagement.magnitude_basis: postprandial active GLP-1 rise; neither abstract gives a fold change, so only direction is compared
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled. Japanese 4-week trial; no ClinicalTrials.gov record found under teneligliptin/MP-513 for this design, so registry_date is null.
engagement.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
engagement.note: Teneligliptin 10 and 20 mg raised postprandial active GLP-1 and cut 2-h postprandial glucose by 29-51 mg/dl in 99 Japanese T2D patients over 4 weeks.
engagement.quote: Both doses of teneligliptin increased postprandial plasma active glucagon-like peptide-1 concentrations compared with placebo.
engagement.judgement: Paired by the drafter: the rat readouts (plasma DPP-4 inhibition, active GLP-1 and insulin after a load) are the readouts Eto 2012 measured in patients, and both moved the same way. Eto's online date (July 2012) precedes the rat paper's (September 2012), so the comparison became public in 2012 and the two entries share a year.

engagement.magnitude_basis: sustained plasma DPP-4 inhibition across the dosing interval; the Biftu 2014 abstract gives no animal percentage to scale against
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; Merck authors. Healthy-subject Phase 1, no registry record found.
engagement.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
engagement.note: Omarigliptin 25 mg weekly held 77-89% plasma DPP-4 inhibition at the 168-h trough and doubled postprandial active GLP-1 in healthy subjects.
engagement.quote: DPP-4 inhibition ranged from ∼77% to 89% at 168 hours following the last of 3 once-weekly doses over the dose range studied.
engagement.reason: GLP-1 and DPP-4 inhibition moved as in rodents
engagement.judgement: Second member on the same track (omarigliptin, lean-mouse/dog/monkey pharmacology in Biftu 2014); added as strengthens because the status does not change. Prusogliptin later reproduced the pattern in patients (62-89% DPP-4 inhibition, Clin Pharmacokinet 2025, doi:10.1007/s40262-025-01501-8, NCT05146869).

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper states no tolerability margin, so margin_stated stays null.
dose.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
dose.note: Teneligliptin was active from 0.1 mg/kg in Zucker fatty rats and 1 mg/kg covered 12 h; rat plasma DPP-4 ED50 0.41 mg/kg; no human dose.
dose.short: Rat ED50 0.41 mg/kg, active from 0.1 mg/kg
dose.quote: An oral carbohydrate-loading test in Zucker fatty rats showed that teneligliptin at ≥ 0.1mg/kg increased the maximum increase in plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 and insulin levels, and reduced glucose excursions.

dose.magnitude_basis: effective oral dose in mg/kg: rat plasma DPP-4 ED50 0.41 mg/kg and Zucker threshold 0.1 mg/kg vs 20 mg once daily (about 0.3 mg/kg at 60 kg) in patients
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled. Registry: NCT00628212 (MP-513 Phase 2, results first posted 2013-05-31); the paper went online 2013-04-07, which sets the year. The mg/kg conversion assumes a 60 kg Japanese patient and is the drafter's.
dose.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
dose.note: Teneligliptin 10-40 mg daily (about 0.17-0.67 mg/kg) all cut HbA1c 0.9-1.0% in 324 patients; the marketed 20 mg sits within 2x of the rat ED50.
dose.quote: Treatment with teneligliptin for 12 weeks provided significant and clinically meaningful reductions in HbA1c and FPG across the dose range studied and was generally well tolerated in Japanese patients with T2DM.
dose.judgement: Called same by the drafter's pairing: the human dose range that lowered HbA1c brackets the rat ED50, and the flat 10-40 mg dose-response matches a target already saturated at the rat threshold. No source states the comparison. margin_stated is null because the rat paper gives no tolerated-dose ceiling, so the toxic end of the window is not scored here.

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: once-weekly projected from non-rodent PK (Biftu 2014) vs once-weekly supported at 25 mg in humans
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both sides; the Biftu 2014 full text (ACS) could not be opened, so the mouse OGTT ED50 and the animal half-lives are not quoted. Merck authors on both.
dose.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
dose.note: Biftu 2014 projected once-weekly dosing from omarigliptin's dog and monkey PK; 25 mg weekly in healthy subjects held 77-89% DPP-4 inhibition over 7 days.
dose.short: Weekly interval projected from dog/monkey PK held
dose.quote: Administration of omarigliptin was generally well tolerated in healthy subjects, and both the PK and PD profiles support once-weekly dosing.
dose.reason: Human dose at rodent ED50; weekly interval held
dose.judgement: Strengthens, second member: the regimen prediction (weekly) rather than a mg/kg target is what the model side states in its abstract. Cofrogliptin's biweekly regimen, projected from monkey DPP-4 inhibition of ~80% through day 14 (Front Pharmacol 2025, doi:10.3389/fphar.2025.1702101), was not scored because that paper appeared after the Phase 3 read out.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the ACS full text with the animal half-lives and the allometric projection could not be opened. Merck authors. model_filed true because the 2015 Marizev review carries the rat and dog PK.
dose.note: Omarigliptin's rat, dog and monkey PK projected a human half-life long enough for once-weekly dosing; no human regimen yet compared.
dose.quote: MK-3102 (omarigliptin), was identified as a potent and selective dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor with an excellent pharmacokinetic profile amenable for once-weekly human dosing and selected as a clinical development candidate.
dose.judgement: Own track per the checker: the regimen prediction comes from non-rodent PK scaled to humans, not from the rodent plasma-DPP-4/OGTT system that the draft's dose index 3 (Krishna 2016) is keyed to. Dose only: the system predicts exposure and interval, not efficacy or harm.
dose.model: Dog and monkey pharmacokinetics scaled allometrically to a human half-life and dosing interval (once-weekly omarigliptin, biweekly cofrogliptin)

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: once-weekly projected from dog/monkey PK vs once-weekly at 25 mg holding 87.5% trough DPP-4 inhibition at 168 h in Japanese healthy adults (P005) and HbA1c superiority at 24 weeks (P020)
dose.confidence_note: Japanese review read via pdftotext; the applicant's dose rationale (審査の概略, 本薬の効果について and (6) 用法・用量) sets rat MRT ~11 h and dog t1/2 ~22 h beside the human alpha 33-50 h / beta ~140 h half-lives and the 87.5% trough inhibition; the allometric step itself is stated in Biftu 2014, not in the review. No tolerated-dose ceiling is stated by the allometry, so margin_stated stays null.
dose.note: Human alpha t1/2 33-50 h, beta ~140 h beside dog 22 h; 25 mg weekly held 87.5% trough DPP-4 inhibition, weekly regimen stood.
dose.short: Weekly interval from animal PK held
dose.quote: 日本人健康成人に本薬 25 mg を週 1 回 3 週間反復経口投与したときの最終投与 168 時間後における本薬未変化体の血漿中非結合形薬物濃度は 8.2 nmol/L、血漿中 DPP-4 活性阻害率は 87.5%であった（P005 試験）。
dose.judgement: The predicted regimen (weekly) was reached and was enough: trough DPP-4 inhibition above the 80% target and a positive 24-week Phase 3 at that interval. The draft's dose index 3 (Krishna 2016, tier 1) is this comparison on the wrong track; it should be re-keyed to this model_id rather than duplicated, so no 2016 entry is added here.
dose.model: Dog and monkey pharmacokinetics scaled allometrically to a human half-life and dosing interval (once-weekly omarigliptin, biweekly cofrogliptin)

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval: monkey DPP-4 inhibition ~80% through day 14 after 10 mg/kg plus allometric scaling vs the biweekly 10/25 mg regimen that lowered HbA1c 0.63/0.59% at week 24 (NCT04556851)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level, open access; sponsor (Haisco) authors. Published 2026-01-05, after the Phase 3 (Gao 2025, doi:10.1111/dom.16014; NCT04556851, no results posted) read out. The monkey work is IND-enabling pharmacology run before the clinic, so scored prospective (retrodiction false) and dated at publication (decision 7); this is the checker's rule question 4, and if read as a retrodiction the status becomes retro. model_filed null: the Chinese NMPA review is not public.
dose.note: Cofrogliptin 10 mg/kg held ~80% monkey DPP-4 inhibition through day 14; allometry predicted the biweekly regimen that lowered HbA1c in Phase 3.
dose.quote: Based on allometric scaling analyses, cofrogliptin is predicted to display superior human pharmacokinetic properties relative to MK3102, with anticipated longer-acting features that align with its clinical dosing frequency.
dose.reason: Animal PK set the interval that held
dose.judgement: Second member on the track, status unchanged. The draft dropped this because the paper post-dates the Phase 3; v3 dates by public date, so it is entered as strengthens with the retrodiction question flagged rather than left out.
dose.model: Dog and monkey pharmacokinetics scaled allometrically to a human half-life and dosing interval (once-weekly omarigliptin, biweekly cofrogliptin)

efficacy.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
efficacy.note: Two weeks of teneligliptin lowered glucose excursions after a carbohydrate load and non-fasting triglycerides in Zucker fatty rats; no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.short: 2-week dosing cut glucose excursions in Zucker rats
efficacy.quote: In Zucker fatty rats, repeated administration of teneligliptin for two weeks reduced glucose excursions in the oral carbohydrate-loading test and decreased the plasma levels of triglycerides and free fatty acids under non-fasting conditions.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of glycaemic lowering; rat glucose-excursion AUC and human HbA1c are different quantities
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; NCT00628212 results first posted 2013-05-31, after the 2013-04-07 online date.
efficacy.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
efficacy.note: 12-week placebo-controlled dose-ranging: teneligliptin 10-40 mg cut HbA1c 0.9-1.0% and FPG 17-20 mg/dl (primary endpoint HbA1c) in 324 Japanese patients.
efficacy.quote: All teneligliptin-treated groups showed significantly greater reductions in HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) than did the placebo group.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by the drafter, not stated by either source. Same rather than neg: no member that worked in the rodent assay later failed on HbA1c, and melogliptin (GRC 8200), the one member that stopped (Phase 2 NCT00836940, no results), has no public rodent or patient efficacy data to judge against the class bar.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of glycaemic lowering; the Biftu 2014 abstract gives no mouse OGTT number
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access abstract with numbers; NCT01217073 results first posted 2015-10-29, after the 2015-08-26 online date. Merck authors.
efficacy.model: Rodent plasma DPP-4 inhibition and oral glucose/carbohydrate load (Wistar and Zucker fatty rats; lean, DIO, db/db mice)
efficacy.note: Omarigliptin 0.25-25 mg once weekly gave dose-related HbA1c reductions over 12 weeks in 685 patients; 25 mg -0.72% vs placebo (primary endpoint HbA1c).
efficacy.quote: Once-weekly treatment for 12 weeks with omarigliptin provided dose-related reductions in HbA1c, 2-h PMG, and FPG.
efficacy.judgement: Second member on the rodent track, status unchanged. Later Phase 3s for omarigliptin, prusogliptin, cofrogliptin and retagliptin all lowered HbA1c 0.4-0.8% vs placebo and are listed in patient_trials; the NCT pairings for the three Chinese programmes are by title (the abstracts give no NCT) and no results are posted for them.

patient_trials.quote: In people with T2DM, omarigliptin monotherapy improved glycemic control over 54 weeks and was generally well tolerated with a low risk of hypoglycemia.

DBPR108 as add-on therapy to metformin offered a significant improvement in glycaemic control, was superior to metformin monotherapy (placebo) and was safe and well-tolerated in patients with T2D that is inadequately controlled with metformin.
The mean treatment difference between DBPR108 and placebo was -0.61% (95% CI -0.77% to -0.44%), and between DBPR108 and sitagliptin was -0.03% (95% CI -0.19% to 0.13%).

At week 24, the least-squares (LS) mean difference (95% confidence interval [CI]) in HbA1c versus placebo was -0.63% (-0.81, -0.46) with cofrogliptin 10 mg and -0.59% (-0.77, -0.42) with cofrogliptin 25 mg (both p < 0.0001).

At week 16, the least squares mean change in HbA1c from baseline, compared with placebo, was -0.82% (95% CI, -1.05% to -0.58%) for the retagliptin 100 mg QD group (P < .0001) per treatment policy estimand.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change predicted vs observed; the abstract says the profiles matched but gives no numbers
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; sponsor (Haisco) authors, first author Cui C. Validating trials NCT04556851 and NCT04564872 have no posted results, so registry_date is null. The Phase 2b waiver is stated in the abstract.
efficacy.model: Population PK/PD plus model-based meta-analysis (cofrogliptin single-ascending-dose data to DPP-4 inhibition to HbA1c)
efficacy.note: Cofrogliptin's PopPK/PD-MBMA model, built on healthy-subject SAD data, predicted the biweekly DPP-4 inhibition and HbA1c profiles later seen in T2D patients.
efficacy.quote: The PK/DPP-4 inhibition/HbA1c profiles of T2D patients treated with HSK7653 matched the modelled data.
efficacy.reason: HbA1c fell as rodents and PK/PD model predicted
efficacy.judgement: A second track because it is a different system: an in-silico human PK/PD model, not an animal. Prospective, not a retrodiction: the prediction was made from Phase 1 data and the Phase 2b waiver granted before the Phase 3 read out. model_first_use_year is the publication year; the model was built earlier but no earlier public date exists. The alternative reading is that clinical-pharmacology modelling is not a model system for this atlas, in which case this entry is dropped and the cell stands on the rodent track.

safety.magnitude_basis: QTc prolongation risk at clinical exposure (predicted low, observed none); no ms values in the abstract
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled, Merck authors; the thorough QT trial is not cited by registry number in the abstract. Low because this is clinical-pharmacology modelling rather than a preclinical model.
safety.model: Concentration-QTc model from the omarigliptin single-ascending-dose study
safety.note: A C-QTc model fitted to omarigliptin's SAD data predicted low QTc-prolongation risk at clinical doses; a thorough QT trial later confirmed it.
safety.short: C-QTc forecast confirmed in thorough QT
safety.quote: A model-based assessment of QTc interval risk from the single ascending dose study predicted a low risk of QTc prolongation within the likely clinical dose range, a finding later confirmed in a thorough QT trial.
safety.judgement: Scored same because the model made a stated prediction (low QTc risk) that held in a dedicated trial, and in_silico is an admissible model_kind. Cofrogliptin's C-QTc model (doi:10.1002/cpdd.1418) predicted the same but no confirming study is cited, so it is not scored. If the reviewer reads human-data models as out of scope, drop this track and the safety cell is untested only.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The Japanese (teneligliptin 2012, omarigliptin 2015) and Chinese (prusogliptin, cofrogliptin, retagliptin) review documents that hold the tox packages were not retrieved; the 2021 paper is the earliest member tox statement found in English.
safety.model: Animal pharmacology and toxicology (rat, dog, mouse) behind the members' approvals
safety.note: Prusogliptin's rat, dog and diabetic-mouse pharmacology claims 'good safety profiles in animals' and names no harm; no member tox package set against a patient harm.
safety.quote: DBPR108 is a novel DPP-4-selective inhibitor of small molecule that demonstrated potent in vivo pharmacological effects and good safety profiles in animals.
safety.judgement: Untested, not empty: tox packages existed for every approved member but nothing public compares them with patients. Patient-side facts with no model side: omarigliptin's early-terminated CVOT (NCT01703208, results 2017-12-12, doi:10.1186/s12933-017-0593-8) found MACE HR 1.00 and hHF HR 0.60 (no harm to compare); retagliptin's Phase 3 saw slightly more lipase and amylase rises (doi:10.1111/dom.15601); teneligliptin's Japanese label QT caution at 160 mg rests on a thorough-QT study whose nonclinical hERG/dog counterpart could not be found. The class pancreatitis and heart-failure questions were raised on sitagliptin and saxagliptin, which are not members.
safety.reason: QTc forecast held; class harms never compared

safety.confidence_note: Read from the English PMDA review (3.(iii).A.(2).5)-(2).6), pdftotext); the study reports 4.2.3.2-7/-8 are not public. The review is dated 2012-04-05; the application was filed 2011-08-26.
safety.note: Teneligliptin 75-100 mg/kg/day gave necrotic dermatosis of auricle and tail in cynomolgus monkeys (13- and 52-week studies); NOAEL 30 mg/kg/day, 13-25x clinical AUC.
safety.quote: One male and 2 females in the 75 mg/kg/day showed necrotic dermatosis in the auricle, tail, etc., and in these animals, teneligliptin was withdrawn or administered in reduced dose from Day 40.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. Its own track: the draft's animal-tox-package track is rat, dog and mouse on a prusogliptin paper and names no monkey and no harm; this is a named species-specific finding with its own mechanism literature (DPP-8/9 inhibition, Lankas 2005 rat/dog syndrome cited via the Januvia package).
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13- and 52-week repeat-dose toxicity (necrotic dermatosis at the extremities, the DPP-8/9-linked cutaneous toxicity of the gliptin class)

safety.magnitude_basis: predicted harm (necrotic dermatosis) vs its incidence in the Japanese and foreign teneligliptin trials: none
safety.confidence_note: Tier 2, English review text. The same review's 3.(iii).B.(3) concludes the skin toxicity 'is most likely to be unique only to monkeys' and PMDA accepted it; the package insert still cautions that it was seen in monkeys.
safety.note: No necrotic dermatosis or serious skin reaction in any teneligliptin trial; applicant and PMDA call the monkey skin toxicity species-specific (DPP-8/9 class finding).
safety.short: Monkey skin harm absent in patients
safety.quote: Necrotic dermatosis observed in the oral toxicity study in monkeys and serious hypersensitivity reactions observed with drugs of the same class were not observed in any of the clinical studies.
safety.reason: Predicted skin necrosis never appeared in patients
safety.judgement: Decision 5 canonical case: the regulator itself calls the predicted harm species-specific, so contra with magnitude opposite. product_in_model true because teneligliptin was dosed; the vildagliptin/saxagliptin monkey data and the Januvia DPP-8/9 package are the mechanism source only. Not changed by later labels: pemphigoid entered the teneligliptin (2016-11-22) and omarigliptin (2018-04-19) labels, a different pathology the monkeys did not show (checker rule question 2), and omarigliptin's 3-month monkey study (9 mg/kg/day, 48x AUC) was silent on skin with no necrotic dermatosis in its trials, a same that cannot turn a contra track back. The checker proposed correcting the draft's animal-tox-package 2021 entry from this same finding; the merger should carry it on one track only.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13- and 52-week repeat-dose toxicity (necrotic dermatosis at the extremities, the DPP-8/9-linked cutaneous toxicity of the gliptin class)

safety.confidence_note: English review 3.(i).A.(3).2) and 3.(i).B.(2), pdftotext; the quote is PMDA's own summary of the package (hERG IC50 3.45 uM, guinea-pig papillary muscle APD NOEL 4x, monkey and dog QTc prolongation).
safety.note: Teneligliptin hERG IC50 3.45 uM (15x unbound Cmax at 40 mg); monkey QTc prolongation at 30 mg/kg, NOEL 10 mg/kg (17x); dog 7 mg/kg i.v.
safety.quote: In vitro and in vivo studies on teneligliptin show effects suggestive of QTc interval prolongation.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Its own track: a safety-pharmacology system (ion channel plus non-rodent ECG), distinct from the draft's in-silico C-QTc track and from the generic rat/dog/mouse tox track.
safety.model: hERG channel assay plus dog and monkey ECG/telemetry (QTc) safety pharmacology

safety.magnitude_basis: exposure multiple of the 40 mg unbound Cmax at which QTc prolongation appears: model NOEL 17x (monkey) and hERG IC50 15x vs the 160 mg thorough-QT arm at about 4.5x the 40 mg Cmax (2259 vs 499.7 ng/mL)
safety.confidence_note: Tier 2; the applicant's response in 3.(i).B.(2) puts the hERG/monkey/dog data and the thorough-QT result in one paragraph, and PMDA's 4.(iii).B.(3).7) attributes the human QTc prolongation to hERG inhibition by the parent drug. Thorough-QT study MP-513-A01 has no registry record found; dates are redacted in the review.
safety.note: Thorough QT (MP-513-A01): ddQTcI 9.3 [5.6, 13.0] ms at 160 mg near tmax, 3.9 [0.2, 7.6] ms at 40 mg; PMDA ties it to hERG.
safety.short: QTc rose at 160 mg as hERG predicted
safety.quote: In addition, in the Thorough QT/QTc study, QTc interval prolongation was observed only time points near tmax after administration of teneligliptin 160 mg, and no clinically significant QTc interval prolongation was observed at 40 mg
safety.judgement: Predicted harm appeared, at a supratherapeutic dose: same in direction, margin about 4x narrower than the animal NOEL. Counted once, here in safety; no dose-ceiling entry is made on this track (decision 16, checker rule question 3), and the 40 mg maximum dose was clean, so the Japanese label carries a QT caution rather than a dose restriction.
safety.model: hERG channel assay plus dog and monkey ECG/telemetry (QTc) safety pharmacology

safety.magnitude_basis: QTc risk at clinical exposure: no effect predicted below 40.8x unbound Cmax (dog telemetry NOEL) and 76.9x (hERG IC20); the thorough-QT at 7x the clinical dose gave max ddQTcP 3.66 ms; the human multiple is not given on the unbound basis
safety.confidence_note: Japanese review read via pdftotext (nonclinical 2) 心血管系 and clinical (6) QT/QTc 評価試験 P010); the quote is the contiguous span of the TQT sentence after the footnote marker 52 ('心電図について、第 1 日目に本薬 25 mg、第 2 日目に本薬 175 mg を投与したときの QTcP 間隔 ...'), and the sentence continues 'msec であり、信頼区間の上限が 10 msec を下回った'. comparison_stated false because the review states the animal margins against clinical Cmax but does not itself set them beside the thorough-QT result; model side is the same document. P010 has no registry record found.
safety.note: Omarigliptin hERG IC50 105 uM; dog telemetry QT/QTc up only at 75 mg/kg (NOEL 40.8x); thorough QT 175 mg: ddQTcP 3.66 ms.
safety.quote: ベースラインからの変化量のプラセボ群との差の最大値とその 90%信頼区間は 3.66［1.56, 5.76］
safety.reason: Animal QT margins held in thorough-QT studies
safety.judgement: Second member, status unchanged: the model predicted no QTc liability at clinical exposure with a stated 40.8x margin, and the thorough-QT at 175 mg (7x the 25 mg dose) showed no clinically relevant prolongation. The draft credits omarigliptin's QT only to the in-silico C-QTc model (Krishna 2016); the filed basis was this animal package.
safety.model: hERG channel assay plus dog and monkey ECG/telemetry (QTc) safety pharmacology
